# Debugging Checklist {#sec-debugging}

## Find the stage that needs attention

Use **Build the scene structure → Style the scene → Program game behavior** to narrow down a problem. Check the earlier stages before changing a rule that depends on them.

| Stage | Ask | Try |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build the scene structure | Does the needed element or world object exist? | Check HTML IDs, file paths, object positions, and level data. |
| Style the scene | Is it visible and readable? | Check size, color, display rules, camera, lighting, and hitbox overlays. |
| Program game behavior | Is the action received and the state updated? | Log input and values; trace one update; check collision, scoring, and restart. |

Predict the result of your fix, change one thing, and compare what happens with your prediction.

- [ ] Open the browser developer console and read the first error.
- [ ] Check spelling and capitalization. JavaScript is case-sensitive.
- [ ] Check matching pairs: ( ), { }, [ ], and quote marks.
- [ ] Check whether the element ID in JavaScript exactly matches the HTML id.
- [ ] Use `console.log(...)` to inspect a value.
- [ ] Change one thing at a time, then test again.
- [ ] If you copied code, type the suspicious line yourself and explain each part.
